host_source = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve()
        guest_source = host_source.with_name("vm-guest-probe.py")
        guest_bytes = guest_source.read_bytes()
        host_artifact = run_dir / "executed-host-script.py"
        guest_artifact = run_dir / "executed-guest-probe.py"
        shutil.copy2(host_source, host_artifact)
        guest_artifact.write_bytes(guest_bytes)
        provenance = {
            "source_commit": source_commit,
            "host_script": {"artifact": host_artifact.name,
                            "sha256": sha256_file(host_artifact)},
            "guest_script": {"artifact": guest_artifact.name,
                             "sha256": sha256_file(guest_artifact)},
evidence.reason: The run accepts a syntactically valid --source-commit and records it as provenance, but the executed host script is copied from the current __file__ and the guest script is read from the working tree; the recorded hashes are of those local bytes. Nothing verifies that the working-tree bytes match the supplied commit, so provenance can claim HEAD while executing modified scripts. This is an implementation correctness defect in the existing provenance behavior, not a request for new scope.
